page.overview:
Who is Enda?

Enda was a Celtic teenager, a character from the novelization of .

Enda was a fifteen-year-old Celtic boy who lived in North Ireland during the dawn of the Celtic age around the year 500 BC. He was deformed as he had a twitching mouth and shriveled arm, which was the result of the midwives botching his birth. As a result, he was treated unkindly by his father, brother and uncle, and was the subject of cruel laughter in his village.

At some unknown point, Enda fell in love with the princess Deirdre. When he heard that her father, King Gwynwyll, was offering her hand in marriage, he asked him if he could be the one to marry her. However, Gwynwyll cruelly laughed at the mere idea, as did Enda's father, brother and uncle, who said that Deirdre would rather marry their goat. Instead, Deirdre was betrothed to Cullain, a prince from the Isle of Man.

Not giving up hope, Enda believed that if he could get to Deirdre, then she would like to marry him. However, when Enda went to meet her at the river as she collected water, she misunderstood his motives, became frightened, and almost fell in. Enda then tried to rescue her, but Deirdre believed that he was trying to rape her and fled, accusing him of trying to do so.
